tinker\_cookbook.renderers.Renderer
===================================

_class_ [**tinker\_cookbook.renderers.Renderer**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1322)(_ABC_)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Abstract base class for rendering message lists into training and sampling prompts.

**Subclasses must implement:**

*   get\_stop\_sequences(): Return stop tokens/strings for sampling
*   render\_message(): Break a message into header/output/stop\_overlap components
*   parse\_response(): Convert sampled tokens back into a Message

The default build\_generation\_prompt and build\_supervised\_example implementations assume simple concatenation of rendered messages. Override these if your renderer modifies the conversation structure (e.g., stripping thinking blocks from history).

Pickle support: Renderers created via `get_renderer()` are automatically pickleable. On deserialization, the tokenizer and image processor are reconstructed from cached loaders, so the cost is negligible. Renderers created directly (not via `get_renderer()`) must set `_renderer_name` and `_model_name` manually to be pickleable.

Implementations of [`EnvGroupBuilder`](../../rl/envgroupbuilder/) must be pickleable to support distributed rollout execution. Since many builders store a Renderer, this pickle support is critical.

**Fields:**

*   [**tokenizer**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1344) (_Tokenizer_)
*   [**disables\_thinking**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1346) (_bool_, default: `False`) – Whether this renderer's generation prompt closes the think block.
    
    A closed block tells the model not to reason::
    
    `qwen3                   ...assistant\n<think>\n                 open, so False qwen3_disable_thinking  ...assistant\n<think>\n\n</think>\n\n  closed, so True`
    
    Set it on any renderer that does that. Forgetting is caught by `test_a_turn_that_reasoned_is_never_trained_after_a_prompt_it_cannot_follow`.
    
    DeepSeek's non-thinking renderer does not set it and does not need to: it strips reasoning out of the content, so its render already matches its prompt. - [**supports\_streaming**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1453) (_bool_, default: `False`) – Whether this renderer supports streaming response parsing.
    
    Renderers that set this to True get a default parse\_response\_streaming implementation using ReasoningStreamingParser. They must also define `_end_message_token` and `_parse_response_for_streaming`.
    

### _property_ [**has\_extension\_property**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1391)

Whether this renderer satisfies the sequence extension property.

A renderer has the extension property if, for any multi-turn conversation, calling build\_generation\_prompt at each successive assistant turn produces token sequences where each is a prefix of the next. This enables:

*   Merging multiple timesteps into a single training datum
*   KV-cache reuse during sampling
*   O(T) compute scaling instead of O(T^2) for T-turn trajectories

Renderers that strip thinking blocks from history (like Qwen3Renderer with strip\_thinking\_from\_history=True) do NOT have this property because the observation at timestep 2 is not a prefix of timestep 1's full sequence.

See the Tinker documentation on sequence extension for details.

**Returns:** _bool_

### [**get\_stop\_sequences**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1414)()

Return stop token IDs or strings that signal end-of-generation for the model.

**Returns:** _list\[str\] | list\[int\]_

_Abstract method._

### [**render\_message**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1419)(_message_, _ctx_)

Render a single message into its header/output/stop\_overlap components.

This method breaks down a message into parts for loss masking. See RenderedMessage for detailed semantics of each component.

**Parameters:**

*   [**message**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1419) (_[Message](../message/)_) – The message to render.
*   [**ctx**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1419) (_[RenderContext](../rendercontext/)_) – Context about the message's position in the conversation, including index, is\_last flag, and prev\_message.

**Returns:** _RenderedMessage_ – Container with header, output, and optionally stop\_overlap components for loss masking.

_Abstract method._

### [**parse\_response**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1438)(_response_)

Parse sampled tokens back into a Message.

**Parameters:**

*   [**response**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1438) (_list\[int\]_) – Token IDs returned from sampling.

**Returns:** _tuple\[[Message](../message/), ParseTermination\]_ – A `(message, termination)` tuple. `termination` is an explicit signal — see `ParseTermination`. A best-effort [`Message`](../message/) is always returned, even on `MALFORMED`, so callers can still log / display partial output.

_Abstract method._

### [**parse\_response\_streaming**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1497)(_response_)

Parse response tokens with streaming, yielding incremental deltas.

This enables real-time display of model output by yielding partial content as tokens arrive, rather than waiting for the complete response.

Renderers that set `supports_streaming = True` get a default implementation using ReasoningStreamingParser. Others raise NotImplementedError.

**Parameters:**

*   [**response**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1497) (_list\[int\]_) – Token IDs from the model.

**Returns:** _Iterator\[MessageDelta\]_

### [**to\_openai\_message**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1530)(_message_)

Convert a Message to OpenAI chat completions API format.

The returned object can be passed into the transformers library's apply\_chat\_template function, which is useful for testing purposes.

It's also useful for querying models that are being served through OpenAI-compatible APIs (OpenRouter, vLLM, etc.).

**The base implementation handles:**

*   Basic role/content conversion
*   tool\_calls conversion from ToolCall objects to OpenAI dict format
*   tool\_call\_id and name for tool response messages

Subclasses should override this to handle model-specific features like reasoning\_content for thinking models.

**Parameters:**

*   [**message**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1530) (_[Message](../message/)_) – The Message to convert.

**Returns:** _dict_ – A dict in OpenAI API message format.

### [**create\_conversation\_prefix\_with\_tools**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1602)(_tools_, _system\_prompt_)

Create message(s) with tool specifications to prepend to conversations.

Returns one or more messages to prepend to the conversation. This is the standard way to add tools - the returned messages should be placed at the start of your message list before user/assistant messages.

**Parameters:**

*   [**tools**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1603) (_list\[ToolSpec\]_) – List of tool specifications.
*   [**system\_prompt**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1603) (_str_) – The system prompt content.

**Returns:** _list\[[Message](../message/)\]_ – List of messages to prepend to the conversation.

**Raises:**

*   NotImplementedError: If the renderer doesn't support tool calling.

### [**build\_generation\_prompt**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1647)(_messages_, _role_, _prefill_)

Convert a message list to a token prompt for sampling.

**Parameters:**

*   [**messages**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1648) (_list\[[Message](../message/)\]_) – A list of messages to render.
*   [**role**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1648) (_Role_) – The role of the partial message to be completed. Defaults to `"assistant"`.
*   [**prefill**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1648) (_str | None_) – An optional string to prefill in the model's generation. Useful for constraining the start of the model's output.

**Returns:** _tinker.[ModelInput](../../../../tinker/api-reference/types/modelinput/)_ – A ModelInput containing the tokenized prompt.

### [**build\_supervised\_examples**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1713)(_messages_, _train\_on\_what_)

Build tokens and per-token weights for supervised fine-tuning.

Returns a list of (model\_input, weights) tuples. Multiple examples are needed when the renderer does not satisfy the extension property: it writes an assistant message one way as history and another as the turn being produced, so a single sequence cannot show every turn the context it was sampled from. One example per trained message can, each ending at the message it trains.

**Parameters:**

*   [**messages**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1715) (_list\[[Message](../message/)\]_) – The conversation to render.
*   [**train\_on\_what**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1716) (_[TrainOnWhat](../trainonwhat/)_) – Which parts of the sequence to compute loss on.

**Returns:** _list\[tuple\[tinker.[ModelInput](../../../../tinker/api-reference/types/modelinput/), torch.Tensor\]\]_ – A list of `(ModelInput, weight_tensor)` tuples for training.

### [**build\_supervised\_example**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1761)(_messages_, _train\_on\_what_)

Build tokens and per-token weights for supervised fine-tuning.

This default implementation concatenates rendered messages in order. Override this method if your build\_generation\_prompt does anything that breaks the simple concatenation assumption—for example, if it strips thinking blocks from history (like Qwen3Renderer), injects default system prompts (like KimiK2Renderer), or otherwise modifies the token sequence.

The supervised example tokens should match what build\_generation\_prompt would produce for the same conversation prefix, so the model trains on the same distribution it sees at inference time.

**Parameters:**

*   [**messages**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1763) (_list\[[Message](../message/)\]_) – A list of messages to render.
*   [**train\_on\_what**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1764) (_[TrainOnWhat](../trainonwhat/)_) – Controls which tokens receive non-zero training weight:

**Returns:** _tuple\[tinker.[ModelInput](../../../../tinker/api-reference/types/modelinput/), torch.Tensor\]_ – A `(model_input, weights)` tuple where weights is a 1-D float tensor with the same length as the total number of tokens.

tinker\_cookbook.renderers.Renderer
===================================

_class_ [**tinker\_cookbook.renderers.Renderer**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1322)(_ABC_)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Abstract base class for rendering message lists into training and sampling prompts.

**Subclasses must implement:**

*   get\_stop\_sequences(): Return stop tokens/strings for sampling
*   render\_message(): Break a message into header/output/stop\_overlap components
*   parse\_response(): Convert sampled tokens back into a Message

The default build\_generation\_prompt and build\_supervised\_example implementations assume simple concatenation of rendered messages. Override these if your renderer modifies the conversation structure (e.g., stripping thinking blocks from history).

Pickle support: Renderers created via `get_renderer()` are automatically pickleable. On deserialization, the tokenizer and image processor are reconstructed from cached loaders, so the cost is negligible. Renderers created directly (not via `get_renderer()`) must set `_renderer_name` and `_model_name` manually to be pickleable.

Implementations of [`EnvGroupBuilder`](../../rl/envgroupbuilder/) must be pickleable to support distributed rollout execution. Since many builders store a Renderer, this pickle support is critical.

**Fields:**

*   [**tokenizer**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1344) (_Tokenizer_)
*   [**disables\_thinking**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1346) (_bool_, default: `False`) – Whether this renderer's generation prompt closes the think block.
    
    A closed block tells the model not to reason::
    
    `qwen3                   ...assistant\n<think>\n                 open, so False qwen3_disable_thinking  ...assistant\n<think>\n\n</think>\n\n  closed, so True`
    
    Set it on any renderer that does that. Forgetting is caught by `test_a_turn_that_reasoned_is_never_trained_after_a_prompt_it_cannot_follow`.
    
    DeepSeek's non-thinking renderer does not set it and does not need to: it strips reasoning out of the content, so its render already matches its prompt. - [**supports\_streaming**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1453) (_bool_, default: `False`) – Whether this renderer supports streaming response parsing.
    
    Renderers that set this to True get a default parse\_response\_streaming implementation using ReasoningStreamingParser. They must also define `_end_message_token` and `_parse_response_for_streaming`.
    

### _property_ [**has\_extension\_property**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1391)

Whether this renderer satisfies the sequence extension property.

A renderer has the extension property if, for any multi-turn conversation, calling build\_generation\_prompt at each successive assistant turn produces token sequences where each is a prefix of the next. This enables:

*   Merging multiple timesteps into a single training datum
*   KV-cache reuse during sampling
*   O(T) compute scaling instead of O(T^2) for T-turn trajectories

Renderers that strip thinking blocks from history (like Qwen3Renderer with strip\_thinking\_from\_history=True) do NOT have this property because the observation at timestep 2 is not a prefix of timestep 1's full sequence.

See the Tinker documentation on sequence extension for details.

**Returns:** _bool_

Return stop token IDs or strings that signal end-of-generation for the model.

**Returns:** _list\[str\] | list\[int\]_

_Abstract method._

### [**render\_message**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1419)(_message_, _ctx_)

Render a single message into its header/output/stop\_overlap components.

This method breaks down a message into parts for loss masking. See RenderedMessage for detailed semantics of each component.

**Parameters:**

*   [**message**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1419) (_[Message](../message/)_) – The message to render.
*   [**ctx**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1419) (_[RenderContext](../rendercontext/)_) – Context about the message's position in the conversation, including index, is\_last flag, and prev\_message.

**Returns:** _RenderedMessage_ – Container with header, output, and optionally stop\_overlap components for loss masking.

_Abstract method._

### [**parse\_response**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1438)(_response_)

Parse sampled tokens back into a Message.

**Parameters:**

*   [**response**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1438) (_list\[int\]_) – Token IDs returned from sampling.

**Returns:** _tuple\[[Message](../message/), ParseTermination\]_ – A `(message, termination)` tuple. `termination` is an explicit signal — see `ParseTermination`. A best-effort [`Message`](../message/) is always returned, even on `MALFORMED`, so callers can still log / display partial output.

_Abstract method._

### [**parse\_response\_streaming**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1497)(_response_)

Parse response tokens with streaming, yielding incremental deltas.

This enables real-time display of model output by yielding partial content as tokens arrive, rather than waiting for the complete response.

Renderers that set `supports_streaming = True` get a default implementation using ReasoningStreamingParser. Others raise NotImplementedError.

**Parameters:**

*   [**response**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1497) (_list\[int\]_) – Token IDs from the model.

**Returns:** _Iterator\[MessageDelta\]_

### [**to\_openai\_message**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1530)(_message_)

Convert a Message to OpenAI chat completions API format.

The returned object can be passed into the transformers library's apply\_chat\_template function, which is useful for testing purposes.

It's also useful for querying models that are being served through OpenAI-compatible APIs (OpenRouter, vLLM, etc.).

**The base implementation handles:**

*   Basic role/content conversion
*   tool\_calls conversion from ToolCall objects to OpenAI dict format
*   tool\_call\_id and name for tool response messages

Subclasses should override this to handle model-specific features like reasoning\_content for thinking models.

**Parameters:**

*   [**message**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1530) (_[Message](../message/)_) – The Message to convert.

**Returns:** _dict_ – A dict in OpenAI API message format.

### [**create\_conversation\_prefix\_with\_tools**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1602)(_tools_, _system\_prompt_)

Create message(s) with tool specifications to prepend to conversations.

Returns one or more messages to prepend to the conversation. This is the standard way to add tools - the returned messages should be placed at the start of your message list before user/assistant messages.

**Parameters:**

*   [**tools**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1603) (_list\[ToolSpec\]_) – List of tool specifications.
*   [**system\_prompt**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1603) (_str_) – The system prompt content.

**Returns:** _list\[[Message](../message/)\]_ – List of messages to prepend to the conversation.

**Raises:**

*   NotImplementedError: If the renderer doesn't support tool calling.

### [**build\_generation\_prompt**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1647)(_messages_, _role_, _prefill_)

Convert a message list to a token prompt for sampling.

**Parameters:**

*   [**messages**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1648) (_list\[[Message](../message/)\]_) – A list of messages to render.
*   [**role**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1648) (_Role_) – The role of the partial message to be completed. Defaults to `"assistant"`.
*   [**prefill**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1648) (_str | None_) – An optional string to prefill in the model's generation. Useful for constraining the start of the model's output.

**Returns:** _tinker.[ModelInput](../../../../tinker/api-reference/types/modelinput/)_ – A ModelInput containing the tokenized prompt.

### [**build\_supervised\_examples**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1713)(_messages_, _train\_on\_what_)

Build tokens and per-token weights for supervised fine-tuning.

Returns a list of (model\_input, weights) tuples. Multiple examples are needed when the renderer does not satisfy the extension property: it writes an assistant message one way as history and another as the turn being produced, so a single sequence cannot show every turn the context it was sampled from. One example per trained message can, each ending at the message it trains.

**Parameters:**

*   [**messages**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1715) (_list\[[Message](../message/)\]_) – The conversation to render.
*   [**train\_on\_what**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1716) (_[TrainOnWhat](../trainonwhat/)_) – Which parts of the sequence to compute loss on.

**Returns:** _list\[tuple\[tinker.[ModelInput](../../../../tinker/api-reference/types/modelinput/), torch.Tensor\]\]_ – A list of `(ModelInput, weight_tensor)` tuples for training.

### [**build\_supervised\_example**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1761)(_messages_, _train\_on\_what_)

Build tokens and per-token weights for supervised fine-tuning.

This default implementation concatenates rendered messages in order. Override this method if your build\_generation\_prompt does anything that breaks the simple concatenation assumption—for example, if it strips thinking blocks from history (like Qwen3Renderer), injects default system prompts (like KimiK2Renderer), or otherwise modifies the token sequence.

The supervised example tokens should match what build\_generation\_prompt would produce for the same conversation prefix, so the model trains on the same distribution it sees at inference time.

**Parameters:**

*   [**messages**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1763) (_list\[[Message](../message/)\]_) – A list of messages to render.
*   [**train\_on\_what**](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tinker_cookbook/renderers/base.py#L1764) (_[TrainOnWhat](../trainonwhat/)_) – Controls which tokens receive non-zero training weight:

**Returns:** _tuple\[tinker.[ModelInput](../../../../tinker/api-reference/types/modelinput/), torch.Tensor\]_ – A `(model_input, weights)` tuple where weights is a 1-D float tensor with the same length as the total number of tokens.

Tutorial 201: Rendering
=======================

Prerequisites

*   [Your First SFT](../../basics/first-sft/)

Run it interactively [\[source\]](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tutorials/201_rendering.py)

`[](#__codelineno-0-1)curl -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/main/tutorials/201_rendering.py && marimo edit 201_rendering.py`

Rendering converts a list of messages into a token sequence that a model can consume. While similar to HuggingFace chat templates, Tinker's rendering system handles the full training lifecycle: supervised learning, reinforcement learning, and deployment.

The renderer sits between your high-level conversation data and the low-level tokens the model sees:

`[](#__codelineno-1-1)Messages (list of dicts)  -->  Renderer  -->  Token IDs (list of ints)`

This tutorial covers the `Renderer` class and its key methods.

Setup
-----

We need a tokenizer (to map between text and token IDs) and a renderer (to apply the model's chat format). Note for this example that both Qwen3.5 and Qwen3.6 models use the same `qwen3_5` renderer.

`[](#__codelineno-2-1)from tinker_cookbook import renderers, tokenizer_utils [](#__codelineno-2-2) [](#__codelineno-2-3)tokenizer = tokenizer_utils.get_tokenizer("Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B") [](#__codelineno-2-4)renderer = renderers.get_renderer("qwen3_5", tokenizer) [](#__codelineno-2-5)renderer  # noqa: B018`

Example conversation
--------------------

We will use this conversation throughout the tutorial.

**Renderer lookup and names**

- Usage: `renderers.get_renderer(_renderer_name, _tokenizer)`
- Usage: `renderer = renderers.get_renderer("qwen3_5", tokenizer, image_processor=image_processor)`
- The page doesn't give a formal signature. From usage, it takes a name, a tokenizer, and an optional `image_processor` keyword.
- Renderer names listed: `qwen3_5`, `qwen3_5_disable_thinking`, `deepseekv3`, `deepseekv3_thinking`, `nemotron3`, `kimi_k26`, `kimi_k26_disable_thinking`.
- The page says: "Each renderer produces the correct special tokens for its model family."

**Tokenizer**

- Usage: `_tokenizer = tokenizer_utils.get_tokenizer(_model_name)`
- The page doesn't show the import path for `tokenizer_utils`.

**build_generation_prompt**

- Usage: `prompt = renderer.build_generation_prompt(messages[:-1])`
- Comment in the page: "# Remove the last assistant message so the model can generate one"
- Returns a `ModelInput`.

**get_stop_sequences**

- Usage: `stop_sequences = renderer.get_stop_sequences()`
- Returns token IDs (or strings). For Qwen3.5/3.6, the output is `[248046]`, which is `<|im_end|>`.

**parse_response**

- Usage: `parsed_message, termination = renderer.parse_response(fake_tokens)`
- Returns a message dict and a `ParseTermination` enum with values `STOP_SEQUENCE`, `EOS`, and `MALFORMED`.
- Properties: `termination.is_clean` and `termination.is_stop_sequence`.

**build_supervised_example**

- Usage: `model_input, weights = renderer.build_supervised_example(messages)`
- Returns the tokens (`ModelInput`) and per-token loss weights.
- The page says: "Only the final assistant message has weight 1 (completion)."

**TrainOnWhat**

- Usage: `train_on_what=renderers.TrainOnWhat.ALL_ASSISTANT_MESSAGES`
- Values: `LAST_ASSISTANT_MESSAGE` (default), `LAST_ASSISTANT_TURN`, `ALL_ASSISTANT_MESSAGES`, `ALL_MESSAGES`, `ALL_TOKENS`, `CUSTOMIZED`.

**Custom renderers**

- Usage: `renderers.register_renderer("MyOrg/custom_format", my_renderer_factory)`
- The factory takes `(tokenizer, image_processor=None)`.
- Also used: `renderers.get_registered_renderer_names()` and `renderers.unregister_renderer("MyOrg/custom_format")`.

Tutorial 201: Rendering
=======================

Prerequisites

*   [Your First SFT](../../basics/first-sft/)

Run it interactively [\[source\]](https://github.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/blob/main/tutorials/201_rendering.py)

`[](#__codelineno-0-1)curl -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thinking-machines-lab/tinker-cookbook/main/tutorials/201_rendering.py && marimo edit 201_rendering.py`

Rendering converts a list of messages into a token sequence that a model can consume. While similar to HuggingFace chat templates, Tinker's rendering system handles the full training lifecycle: supervised learning, reinforcement learning, and deployment.

The renderer sits between your high-level conversation data and the low-level tokens the model sees:

`[](#__codelineno-1-1)Messages (list of dicts)  -->  Renderer  -->  Token IDs (list of ints)`

This tutorial covers the `Renderer` class and its key methods.

Setup
-----

We need a tokenizer (to map between text and token IDs) and a renderer (to apply the model's chat format). Note for this example that both Qwen3.5 and Qwen3.6 models use the same `qwen3_5` renderer.

`[](#__codelineno-2-1)from tinker_cookbook import renderers, tokenizer_utils [](#__codelineno-2-2) [](#__codelineno-2-3)tokenizer = tokenizer_utils.get_tokenizer("Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B") [](#__codelineno-2-4)renderer = renderers.get_renderer("qwen3_5", tokenizer) [](#__codelineno-2-5)renderer  # noqa: B018`

Example conversation
--------------------

We will use this conversation throughout the tutorial.

`[](#__codelineno-3-1)messages = [ [](#__codelineno-3-2)    {"role": "system", "content": "Answer concisely; at most one sentence per response"}, [](#__codelineno-3-3)    {"role": "user", "content": "What is the longest-lived rodent species?"}, [](#__codelineno-3-4)    {"role": "assistant", "content": "The naked mole rat, which can live over 30 years."}, [](#__codelineno-3-5)    {"role": "user", "content": "How do they live so long?"}, [](#__codelineno-3-6)    { [](#__codelineno-3-7)        "role": "assistant", [](#__codelineno-3-8)        "content": "They evol

**Renderer lookup and names**

- Usage: `renderers.get_renderer(_renderer_name, _tokenizer)`
- Usage: `renderer = renderers.get_renderer("qwen3_5", tokenizer, image_processor=image_processor)`
- The page doesn't give a formal signature. From usage, it takes a name, a tokenizer, and an optional `image_processor` keyword.
- Renderer names listed: `qwen3_5`, `qwen3_5_disable_thinking`, `deepseekv3`, `deepseekv3_thinking`, `nemotron3`, `kimi_k26`, `kimi_k26_disable_thinking`.
- The page says: "Each renderer produces the correct special tokens for its model family."

**Tokenizer**

- Usage: `_tokenizer = tokenizer_utils.get_tokenizer(_model_name)`
- The page doesn't show the import path for `tokenizer_utils`.

**build_generation_prompt**

- Usage: `prompt = renderer.build_generation_prompt(messages[:-1])`
- Comment in the page: "# Remove the last assistant message so the model can generate one"
- Returns a `ModelInput`.

**get_stop_sequences**

- Usage: `stop_sequences = renderer.get_stop_sequences()`
- Returns token IDs (or strings). For Qwen3.5/3.6, the output is `[248046]`, which is `<|im_end|>`.

**parse_response**

- Usage: `parsed_message, termination = renderer.parse_response(fake_tokens)`
- Returns a message dict and a `ParseTermination` enum with values `STOP_SEQUENCE`, `EOS`, and `MALFORMED`.
- Properties: `termination.is_clean` and `termination.is_stop_sequence`.

**build_supervised_example**

- Usage: `model_input, weights = renderer.build_supervised_example(messages)`
- Returns the tokens (`ModelInput`) and per-token loss weights.
- The page says: "Only the final assistant message has weight 1 (completion)."

**TrainOnWhat**

- Usage: `train_on_what=renderers.TrainOnWhat.ALL_ASSISTANT_MESSAGES`
- Values: `LAST_ASSISTANT_MESSAGE` (default), `LAST_ASSISTANT_TURN`, `ALL_ASSISTANT_MESSAGES`, `ALL_MESSAGES`, `ALL_TOKENS`, `CUSTOMIZED`.

**Custom renderers**

- Usage: `renderers.register_renderer("MyOrg/custom_format", my_renderer_factory)`
- The factory takes `(tokenizer, image_processor=None)`.
- Also used: `renderers.get_registered_renderer_names()` and `renderers.unregister_renderer("MyOrg/custom_format")`.

Manage Checkpoints
==================

TrainingClients can save checkpoints for resuming training later, or serving the checkpoint for sampling.

Method

Use it to

Path

[`save_state`](../../api-reference/trainingclient/#save_state)

Resume training

`tinker://<run_id>/weights/<name>`

[`save_weights_for_sampler`](../../api-reference/trainingclient/#save_weights_for_sampler)

Sample, open in the Playground, or download

`tinker://<run_id>/sampler_weights/<name>`

Training checkpoints
--------------------

Save the full training state, including Adam's moment estimates, with `save_state`:

`[](#__codelineno-0-1)checkpoint = training_client.save_state("step-100", user_metadata={ "step": "100", "recipe": "example" }).result() [](#__codelineno-0-2)print(checkpoint.path)  # tinker://<run_id>/weights/step-100 [](#__codelineno-0-3) [](#__codelineno-0-4)# load without optimizer state [](#__codelineno-0-5)training_client = service_client.create_training_client_from_state(checkpoint.path).result() [](#__codelineno-0-6) [](#__codelineno-0-7)# load with optimizer state [](#__codelineno-0-8)training_client = service_client.create_training_client_from_state_with_optimizer(checkpoint.path).result() [](#__codelineno-0-9) [](#__codelineno-0-10)# view checkpoint in Tinker console [](#__codelineno-0-11)print(checkpoint.get_console_url())`

Sampler checkpoints
-------------------

`save_weights_for_sampler` saves only the weights and not gradient or optimizer state for sampling in one of the following ways:

*   Load using [`SamplingClient`](../../api-reference/samplingclient/)
*   Use with [`OpenAI`](../../compatible-apis/openai/) or [`Anthropic`](../../compatible-apis/anthropic/) compatible APIs
*   Chat with in the [Tinker Playground](https://tinker.thinkingmachines.ai/playground)

`[](#__codelineno-1-1)sampler_checkpoint = training_client.save_weights_for_sampler("step-100", user_metadata={ "step": "100", "recipe": "example" }).result() [](#__codelineno-1-2)print(sampler_checkpoint.path)  # tinker://<run_id>/sampler_weights/step-100 [](#__codelineno-1-3) [](#__codelineno-1-4)# load the checkpoint into a sampling client [](#__codelineno-1-5)sampling_client = service_client.create_sampling_client(model_path=sampler_checkpoint.path) [](#__codelineno-1-6) [](#__codelineno-1-7)# chat with checkpoint in Tinker Playground [](#__codelineno-1-8)print(sampler_checkpoint.get_playground_url()) [](#__codelineno-1-9) [](#__codelineno-1-10)# manage checkpoint in Tinker console [](#__codelineno-1-11)print(sampler_checkpoint.get_console_url())`

Expiration
----------

Checkpoint storage is charged at $0.10 per GB per month. To ensure checkpoints are not kept forever, you can set a TTL (time to live) when saving a checkpoint.

`[](#__codelineno-2-1)training_client.save_state("step-100", ttl_seconds=24 * 3600) [](#__codelineno-2-2) [](#__codelineno-2-3)training_client.save_weights_for_sampler("step-100", ttl_seconds=24 * 3600)`

Without a TTL, a checkpoint is kept until you delete it. To change the TTL later, see [Set a TTL](#set-a-ttl) below.

Manage with RestClient
----------------------

Use the [`RestClient`](../../api-reference/restclient/) to manage checkpoints after they are saved.

`[](#__codelineno-3-1)rest_client = service_client.create_rest_client()`

### List checkpoints

`list_checkpoints` lists the checkpoints of a single training run. `list_user_checkpoints` lists them across all of your runs, newest first:

`[](#__codelineno-4-1)response = rest_client.list_checkpoints("<run_id>").result() [](#__codelineno-4-2)for checkpoint in response.checkpoints: [](#__codelineno-4-3)    print(checkpoint.checkpoint_type, checkpoint.tinker_path) [](#__codelineno-4-4) [](#__codelineno-4-5)recent = rest_client.list_user_checkpoints(limit=10).result()`

### Set a TTL

Change or remove a checkpoint's TTL after it is saved:

`[](#__codelineno-5-1)# Expire in 7 days [](#__codelineno-5-2)rest_client.set_checkpoint_ttl_from_tinker_path(path, ttl_seconds=7 * 24 * 3600).result() [](#__codelineno-5-3) [](#__codelineno-5-4)# Keep indefinitely [](#__codelineno-5-5)rest_client.set_checkpoint_ttl_from_tinker_path(path, ttl_seconds=None).result()`

### Publish a checkpoint

Publishing a checkpoint lets other Tinker users load it from its path. Only the owner of the training run can publish or unpublish:

`[](#__codelineno-6-1)rest_client.publish_checkpoint_from_tinker_path(path).result() [](#__codelineno-6-2) [](#__codelineno-6-3)rest_client.unpublish_checkpoint_from_tinker_path(path).result()`

### Download sampler weights

Sampler checkpoints can be downloaded to local disk as a tar file:

`[](#__codelineno-7-1)import tarfile [](#__codelineno-7-2)import urllib.request [](#__codelineno-7-3) [](#__codelineno-7-4)# create a signed url for the checkpoint [](#__codelineno-7-5)archive = rest_client.get_checkpoint_archive_url_from_tinker_path(sampler_checkpoint.path).result() [](#__codelineno-7-6) [](#__codelineno-7-7)# download the checkpoint [](#__codelineno-7-8)urllib.request.urlretrieve(archive.url, "checkpoint.tar") [](#__codelineno-7-9) [](#__codelineno-7-10)# extract the checkpoint [](#__codelineno-7-11)with tarfile.open("checkpoint.tar") as tar: [](#__codelineno-7-12)    tar.extractall("./adapter", filter="data")`

See [`tinker checkpoint download`](../../cli/checkpoint/#checkpoint-download) to download from the CLI.

#### Weights format

The archive holds a LoRA adapter, not a full model. It contains:

*   `adapter_model.safetensors`: the trained LoRA `A` and `B` matrices for each adapted layer, as a [safetensors](https://huggingface.co/docs/safetensors) file.
*   `adapter_config.json`: the LoRA hyperparameters, including the rank `r` and `lora_alpha`. The update applied to each weight is scaled by `lora_alpha / r`.

To use the weights outside Tinker, you need either the adapter merged into the base model's weights or the keys remapped to the PEFT format.

The Tinker Cookbook's [`weights`](../../../cookbook/api-reference/weights/) module provides utilities to download and deploy checkpoints from Tinker. See [Tinker Cookbook Deployment](../../../cookbook/deployment/basics/):

*   [Merge into a HuggingFace Model](../../../cookbook/deployment/export-hf/): one standalone model you can load with `transformers`, vLLM, or SGLang
*   [Build a PEFT LoRA Adapter](../../../cookbook/deployment/lora-adapter/): a lightweight adapter to serve on top of the base model in vLLM or SGLang
*   [Publish to HuggingFace Hub](../../../cookbook/deployment/publish-hub/): upload either one to the Hub

Manage Checkpoints
==================

TrainingClients can save checkpoints for resuming training later, or serving the checkpoint for sampling.

Method

Use it to

Path

[`save_state`](../../api-reference/trainingclient/#save_state)

Resume training

`tinker://<run_id>/weights/<name>`

[`save_weights_for_sampler`](../../api-reference/trainingclient/#save_weights_for_sampler)

Sample, open in the Playground, or download

`tinker://<run_id>/sampler_weights/<name>`

Training checkpoints
--------------------

Save the full training state, including Adam's moment estimates, with `save_state`:

`[](#__codelineno-0-1)checkpoint = training_client.save_state("step-100", user_metadata={ "step": "100", "recipe": "example" }).result() [](#__codelineno-0-2)print(checkpoint.path)  # tinker://<run_id>/weights/step-100 [](#__codelineno-0-3) [](#__codelineno-0-4)# load without optimizer state [](#__codelineno-0-5)training_client = service_client.create_training_client_from_state(checkpoint.path).result() [](#__codelineno-0-6) [](#__codelineno-0-7)# load with optimizer state [](#__codelineno-0-8)training_client = service_client.create_training_client_from_state_with_optimizer(checkpoint.path).result() [](#__codelineno-0-9) [](#__codelineno-0-10)# view checkpoint in Tinker console [](#__codelineno-0-11)print(checkpoint.get_console_url())`

Sampler checkpoints
-------------------

`save_weights_for_sampler` saves only the weights and not gradient or optimizer state for sampling in one of the following ways:

*   Load using [`SamplingClient`](../../api-reference/samplingclient/)
*   Use with [`OpenAI`](../../compatible-apis/openai/) or [`Anthropic`](../../compatible-apis/anthropic/) compatible APIs
*   Chat with in the [Tinker Playground](https://tinker.thinkingmachines.ai/playground)

`[](#__codelineno-1-1)sampler_checkpoint = training_client.save_weights_for_sampler("step-100", user_metadata={ "step": "100", "recipe": "example" }).result() [](#__codelineno-1-2)print(sampler_checkpoint.path)  # tinker://<run_id>/sampler_weights/step-100 [](#__codelineno-1-3) [](#__codelineno-1-4)# load the checkpoint into a sampling client [](#__codelineno-1-5)sampling_client = service_client.create_sampling_client(model_path=sampler_checkpoint.path) [](#__codelineno-1-6) [](#__codelineno-1-7)# chat with checkpoint in Tinker Playground [](#__codelineno-1-8)print(sampler_checkpoint.get_playground_url()) [](#__codelineno-1-9) [](#__codelineno-1-10)# manage checkpoint in Tinker console [](#__codelineno-1-11)print(sampler_checkpoint.get_console_url())`

Expiration
----------

Checkpoint storage is charged at $0.10 per GB per month. To ensure checkpoints are not kept forever, you can set a TTL (time to live) when saving a checkpoint.

`[](#__codelineno-2-1)training_client.save_state("step-100", ttl_seconds=24 * 3600) [](#__codelineno-2-2) [](#__codelineno-2-3)training_client.save_weights_for_sampler("step-100", ttl_seconds=24 * 3600)`

Without a TTL, a checkpoint is kept until you delete it. To change the TTL later, see [Set a TTL](#set-a-ttl) below.

Manage with RestClient
----------------------

Use the [`RestClient`](../../api-reference/restclient/) to manage checkpoints after they are saved.

`[](#__codelineno-3-1)rest_client = service_client.create_rest_client()`

### List checkpoints

`list_checkpoints` lists the checkpoints of a single training run. `list_user_checkpoints` lists them across all of your runs, newest first:

`[](#__codelineno-4-1)response = rest_client.list_checkpoints("<run_id>").result() [](#__codelineno-4-2)for checkpoint in response.checkpoints: [](#__codelineno-4-3)    print(checkpoint.checkpoint_type, checkpoint.tinker_path) [](#__codelineno-4-4) [](#__codelineno-4-5)recent = rest_client.list_user_checkpoints(limit=10).result()`

### Set a TTL

Change or remove a checkpoint's TTL after it is saved:

`[](#__codelineno-5-1)# Expire in 7 days [](#__codelineno-5-2)rest_client.set_checkpoint_ttl_from_tinker_path(path, ttl_seconds=7 * 24 * 3600).result() [](#__codelineno-5-3) [](#__codelineno-5-4)# Keep indefinitely [](#__codelineno-5-5)rest_client.set_checkpoint_ttl_from_tinker_path(path, ttl_seconds=None).result()`

### Publish a checkpoint

Publishing a checkpoint lets other Tinker users load it from its path. Only the owner of the training run can publish or unpublish:

`[](#__codelineno-6-1)rest_client.publish_checkpoint_from_tinker_path(path).result() [](#__codelineno-6-2) [](#__codelineno-6-3)rest_client.unpublish_checkpoint_from_tinker_path(path).result()`

### Download sampler weights

Sampler checkpoints can be downloaded to local disk as a tar file:

`[](#__codelineno-7-1)import tarfile [](#__codelineno-7-2)import urllib.request [](#__codelineno-7-3) [](#__codelineno-7-4)# create a signed url for the checkpoint [](#__codelineno-7-5)archive = rest_client.get_checkpoint_archive_url_from_tinker_path(sampler_checkpoint.path).result() [](#__codelineno-7-6) [](#__codelineno-7-7)# download the checkpoint [](#__codelineno-7-8)urllib.request.urlretrieve(archive.url, "checkpoint.tar") [](#__codelineno-7-9) [](#__codelineno-7-10)# extract the checkpoint [](#__codelineno-7-11)with tarfile.open("checkpoint.tar") as tar: [](#__codelineno-7-12)    tar.extractall("./adapter", filter="data")`

See [`tinker checkpoint download`](../../cli/checkpoint/#checkpoint-download) to download from the CLI.

#### Weights format

The archive holds a LoRA adapter, not a full model. It contains:

*   `adapter_model.safetensors`: the trained LoRA `A` and `B` matrices for each adapted layer, as a [safetensors](https://huggingface.co/docs/safetensors) file.
*   `adapter_config.json`: the LoRA hyperparameters, including the rank `r` and `lora_alpha`. The update applied to each weight is scaled by `lora_alpha / r`.

To use the weights outside Tinker, you need either the adapter merged into the base model's weights or the keys remapped to the PEFT format.

The Tinker Cookbook's [`weights`](../../../cookbook/api-reference/weights/) module provides utilities to download and deploy checkpoints from Tinker. See [Tinker Cookbook Deployment](../../../cookbook/deployment/basics/):

*   [Merge into a HuggingFace Model](../../../cookbook/deployment/export-hf/): one standalone model you can load with `transformers`, vLLM, or SGLang
*   [Build a PEFT LoRA Adapter](../../../cookbook/deployment/lora-adapter/): a lightweight adapter to serve on top of the base model in vLLM or SGLang
*   [Publish to HuggingFace Hub](../../../cookbook/deployment/publish-hub/): upload either one to the Hub

tinker billing
==============

**tinker billing**
------------------

View billing usage.

### tinker billing checkpoint-storage

Show current checkpoint storage and its projected run rate.

With no arguments, returns checkpoint storage usage for the entire authenticated organization, grouped by project and session owner. Use --project-id to limit results to one project within that organization. Checkpoint usage data can lag by 1-2 hours. Monthly costs are gross 720-hour projections using current publicly available rates, before credits and commits; they are not invoice amounts due.

**Options:**

*   `--project-id TEXT` — Only show storage in this project
*   `--csv PATH` — Write storage rows as CSV to PATH instead of table/JSON output ('-' for stdout)

### tinker billing usage _STARTING\_ON_ _ENDING\_BEFORE_

Show hourly billing usage for your organization.

STARTING\_ON and ENDING\_BEFORE are RFC 3339 timestamps aligned to UTC hour boundaries (e.g. 2026-07-13T00:00:00Z), at most 14 days apart. Returns one row per (hour x usage type x base model x session x user), annotated with the project the usage belongs to. Session user metadata comes as a separate per-session table (JSON output / --sessions-csv) to join on session\_id. Quantities are raw tokens / gigabyte-hours. Token and storage rows include estimated gross USD usage cost before credits and commits, plus the applicable effective rate per million tokens or per GB-month. Token cost is the token rate times token\_count / 1,000,000; storage cost is the storage rate times gigabyte\_hours / 720. These are not invoice amounts due. For a completed UTC day, each model/usage-category group is priced only after its full-day quantity reconciles with finalized invoice usage line items, or the latest draft when no finalized invoice is available. Other groups on the same day may remain null. The current incomplete UTC day instead uses the published Tinker rate-card snapshot, so its estimate is not invoice-reconciled and can change after the day completes. Table output renders an unavailable applicable cost or rate as `null`; CSV uses blank cells, while the typed SDK and JSON use null. The SDK response and JSON output also include `cost_data_through`, which marks the exclusive UTC boundary between the two pricing sources: non-null estimates before it use invoice-derived rates, while newer non-null estimates use fixed published rates. A cost or rate may still be null when the data required to price that row is unavailable. `cost_data_through` is null when the response has no completed day with invoice pricing data. Table and CSV output do not include this response-level field. Data lags real time by up to a few hours.

There are no filter flags: export the window once and filter the CSV/JSON client-side.

Requires billing view access in your organization.

**Options:**

*   `--csv PATH` — Write usage rows as CSV to PATH instead of table/JSON output ('-' for stdout)
*   `--sessions-csv PATH` — Also write the per-session side-table (session\_id + user\_metadata) as CSV to PATH ('-' for stdout); join it against the usage rows on session\_id

tinker billing
==============

**tinker billing**
------------------

View billing usage.

### tinker billing checkpoint-storage

Show current checkpoint storage and its projected run rate.

With no arguments, returns checkpoint storage usage for the entire authenticated organization, grouped by project and session owner. Use --project-id to limit results to one project within that organization. Checkpoint usage data can lag by 1-2 hours. Monthly costs are gross 720-hour projections using current publicly available rates, before credits and commits; they are not invoice amounts due.

**Options:**

*   `--project-id TEXT` — Only show storage in this project
*   `--csv PATH` — Write storage rows as CSV to PATH instead of table/JSON output ('-' for stdout)

### tinker billing usage _STARTING\_ON_ _ENDING\_BEFORE_

Show hourly billing usage for your organization.

STARTING\_ON and ENDING\_BEFORE are RFC 3339 timestamps aligned to UTC hour boundaries (e.g. 2026-07-13T00:00:00Z), at most 14 days apart. Returns one row per (hour x usage type x base model x session x user), annotated with the project the usage belongs to. Session user metadata comes as a separate per-session table (JSON output / --sessions-csv) to join on session\_id. Quantities are raw tokens / gigabyte-hours. Token and storage rows include estimated gross USD usage cost before credits and commits, plus the applicable effective rate per million tokens or per GB-month. Token cost is the token rate times token\_count / 1,000,000; storage cost is the storage rate times gigabyte\_hours / 720. These are not invoice amounts due. For a completed UTC day, each model/usage-category group is priced only after its full-day quantity reconciles with finalized invoice usage line items, or the latest draft when no finalized invoice is available. Other groups on the same day may remain null. The current incomplete UTC day instead uses the published Tinker rate-card snapshot, so its estimate is not invoice-reconciled and can change after the day completes. Table output renders an unavailable applicable cost or rate as `null`; CSV uses blank cells, while the typed SDK and JSON use null. The SDK response and JSON output also include `cost_data_through`, which marks the exclusive UTC boundary between the two pricing sources: non-null estimates before it use invoice-derived rates, while newer non-null estimates use fixed published rates. A cost or rate may still be null when the data required to price that row is unavailable. `cost_data_through` is null when the response has no completed day with invoice pricing data. Table and CSV output do not include this response-level field. Data lags real time by up to a few hours.

There are no filter flags: export the window once and filter the CSV/JSON client-side.

Requires billing view access in your organization.

**Options:**

*   `--csv PATH` — Write usage rows as CSV to PATH instead of table/JSON output ('-' for stdout)
*   `--sessions-csv PATH` — Also write the per-session side-table (session\_id + user\_metadata) as CSV to PATH ('-' for stdout); join it against the usage rows on session\_id

NOT READ (so not verified): Datum, ModelInput, TensorData, ForwardBackwardOutput, SampleResponse, SampledSequence, APIFuture, RestClient, the cross-entropy loss page (tinker/losses/cross-entropy/), tutorials/core-concepts/weights (204), tutorials/basics/async-patterns, tinker/under-the-hood, tinker/session-metrics, and cookbook/supervised-learning.

INDEX
- "Supported Models" is shown as "28+" on the index, but the models table lists 36 rows. Qwen/Qwen3-8B is in the table.

1. CLIENT CREATION
- Quickstart and cheatsheet: `import tinker`; `service_client = tinker.ServiceClient()` with comment "# Entry point — reads TINKER_API_KEY from environment".
- ServiceClient signature (API ref): `class tinker.ServiceClient(user_metadata=None, project_id=None, display_name=None, base_url=None, api_key=None, default_headers_overrides=None, **kwargs)`. api_key "Defaults to the `TINKER_API_KEY` environment variable, then to the stored credentials."
- Cheatsheet: `training_client = service_client.create_lora_training_client(base_model="Qwen/Qwen3-8B", rank=32)`
- Full signature: `create_lora_training_client(base_model, rank=32, seed=None, train_mlp=True, train_attn=True, train_unembed=True, user_metadata=None, optimizer=None)` returns TrainingClient. Async variant: `create_lora_training_client_async()`.
- Sampling: `service_client.create_sampling_client(model_path=None, base_model=None, retry_config=None, record_stability_info=False)`. Raises ValueError if neither model_path nor base_model is given. Cheatsheet: `service_client.create_sampling_client(base_model="Qwen/Qwen3-8B")`.
- Also: `training_client.get_tokenizer()` (cheatsheet) and `sampling_client.get_tokenizer()` (SamplingClient API ref, returns PreTrainedTokenizer).
- Quickstart uses `tinker.ServiceClient(display_name="my-first-sft")`, `create_lora_training_client_async(base_model="Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B", rank=16)`.

Is Qwen/Qwen3-8B supported? Yes. The models table row is quoted in the models page summary: "Qwen3-8B | Qwen/Qwen3-8B | 32K | 8B | 8B | Dense | Hybrid". The Tinker ID is `Qwen/Qwen3-8B`. The quickstart does not mention Qwen3-8B; it uses Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B.

2. forward_backward (TrainingClient)
- Signature: `forward_backward(data, loss_fn, loss_fn_config=None)`. Returns: "APIFuture containing the forward/backward outputs, loss, and gradients".
- Cheatsheet: `fwdbwd_future = await training_client.forward_backward_async(data=[datum], loss_fn="cross_entropy")`; `fwdbwd_result = await fwdbwd_future.result_async()`; `print(f"Loss: {fwdbwd_result.loss}")`.
- Non-async form: `training_client.forward_backward(training_data, "cross_entropy")`, then `fwdbwd_future.result()`.
- Other loss strings in cheatsheet: "importance_sampling", "ppo", "cispo", "dro"; custom: `forward_backward_custom_async(data, my_loss_fn)`.
- The result field is `.loss` (quoted in cheatsheet and API ref example). Field names `loss_fn_outputs` and `metrics` and the key `'loss:sum'`: NOT FOUND in pages read. ForwardBackwardOutput page was not read.
- Also `forward(data, loss_fn, loss_fn_config=None)` exists (no gradients).

3. Datum for cross-entropy SFT (cheatsheet, "Prepare training data")
- "A `Datum` is a single training example. It contains input tokens, target tokens, and per-token loss weights (0 = ignore, 1 = compute loss). Position `i` of the input predicts token `i + 1`"
- Code:
  full_sequence = prompt_tokens + completion_tokens
  n_prefix = len(prompt_tokens) - 1
  datum = types.Datum(
      model_input=types.ModelInput.from_ints(tokens=full_sequence[:-1]),
      loss_fn_inputs=dict(
          weights=[0.0] * n_prefix + [1.0] * len(completion_tokens),  # 0 for prompt, 1 for completion
          target_tokens=full_sequence[1:],  # shifted by 1 from input
      )
  )
- So loss_fn_inputs keys are `weights` and `target_tokens`. In the cheatsheet they are plain Python lists of float and int. Whether TensorData or numpy is also accepted is NOT VERIFIED (Datum and TensorData pages not read).
- Note: the renderer's build_supervised_example returns weights as a torch.Tensor (see section 7). The cheatsheet passes lists. Convert with .tolist() if needed (inference).
- RL variant: target_tokens, logprobs, advantages keys.

4. optim_step and AdamParams
- Signature: `optim_step(optim_params=None, adam_params=None)`. Returns "APIFuture containing optimizer step response". adam_params is "a legacy alias and cannot be combined with `optim_params`" [summary].
- Cheatsheet: `await training_client.optim_step_async(types.AdamParams(learning_rate=1e-4))` then `await optim_future.result_async()`. Quickstart: `tinker.AdamParams(learning_rate=2e-4)`.
- AdamParams fields (verbatim field names): learning_rate (float, "Learning rate for the optimizer"), beta1 (float), beta2 (float), eps (float, "Term added to the denominator to improve numerical stability"), weight_decay (float, "Uses decoupled weight decay."), grad_clip_norm (float, "0.0 means no clipping."). Defaults NOT shown on the page.

5. Saving weights
- `training_client.save_weights_for_sampler(name, ttl_seconds=None, user_metadata=None)` returns an APIFuture; result has `.path`. Path format: `tinker://<run_id>/sampler_weights/<name>`. Example: `sampler_checkpoint = training_client.save_weights_for_sampler("step-100", ...).result()`; `print(sampler_checkpoint.path)  # tinker://<run_id>/sampler_weights/step-100`. Async: `save_weights_for_sampler_async(name="first-sft")`.
- `training_client.save_weights_and_get_sampling_client(name=None, retry_config=None, record_stability_info=False)` returns a SamplingClient "configured with the current model weights". Per API ref, `name` is "Deprecated, has no effect. Will be removed in a future release." CONFLICT: the cheatsheet still shows `save_weights_and_get_sampling_client(name="checkpoint-1")`. Treat name as optional and ignored.
- `training_client.save_state(name, ttl_seconds=None, overwrite=False, user_metadata=None)` returns APIFuture with `.path` in `tinker://<run_id>/weights/<name>` (full state incl. optimizer). `load_state(path, weights_access_token=None)` loads weights only.
- Checkpoints howto table: "save_state | Resume training | `tinker://<run_id>/weights/<name>`" and "save_weights_for_sampler | Sample, open in the Playground, or download | `tinker://<run_id>/sampler_weights/<name>`".
- Load for sampling: `service_client.create_sampling_client(model_path=sampler_checkpoint.path)`.
- Resume training: `service_client.create_training_client_from_state(path)` (weights only) and `create_training_client_from_state_with_optimizer(path)`.
- Storage: "Checkpoint storage is charged at $0.10 per GB per month."

6. Sampling
- `sampling_client.sample(prompt, num_samples, sampling_params, include_prompt_logprobs=False, topk_prompt_logprobs=0, topk_sample_logprobs=0, target_prompt_logprobs=None, prompt_alt_tokens_k=0, prompt_logprobs_last_n=None)` returns a Future containing SampleResponse [summary for signature].
- Cheatsheet (async): 
  prompt = types.ModelInput.from_ints(tokenizer.encode("The capital of France is"))
  params = types.SamplingParams(max_tokens=50, temperature=0.7, stop=["\n"])
  result = await sampling_client.sample_async(prompt=prompt, num_samples=1, sampling_params=params)
  print(tokenizer.decode(result.sequences[0].tokens))
- Cheatsheet: "sample_async returns the result directly". Sync form per API ref: `future = sampling_client.sample(prompt=prompt, sampling_params=params, num_samples=1)`; `result = future.result()`.
- SampledSequence fields per quickstart: "Each sample in the result's `sequences` has its `tokens`, the `logprobs` of those tokens, and a `stop_reason`", where stop_reason is "stop" or "length".
- SamplingParams fields (verbatim): max_tokens (Optional[int], "Maximum number of tokens to generate"), seed (Optional[int]), stop (Union[str, Sequence[str], Sequence[int], None], "`None` keeps implicit EOS stopping; `[]` disables all stop tokens, including EOS"), temperature (float), top_k (int, "-1 for no limit"), top_p (float).
- compute_logprobs(prompt, prompt_logprobs_last_n=None) returns a Future of a list; `compute_logprobs_async(prompt)` returns the result directly.

7. Renderers (tinker_cookbook)
- Imports: `from tinker_cookbook import renderers`; `from tinker_cookbook.tokenizer_utils import get_tokenizer`.
- `get_tokenizer(model_name)`: "Get a tokenizer by name." Example: `tokenizer = get_tokenizer("Qwen/Qwen3-8B")`.
- `renderers.get_renderer(name, tokenizer, image_processor, model_name)`: "Factory function to create renderers by name." Parameter `name` docstring list includes: `"qwen3"`: Qwen3 with thinking enabled; `"qwen3_disable_thinking"`: Qwen3 with thinking disabled; `"qwen3_instruct"`: Qwen3 instruct 2507 (no thinking); `"qwen3_8_disable_thinking"`: Qwen3.8 with thinking disabled. image_processor is "Required for VL renderers." Example from docs: `tokenizer = get_tokenizer("Qwen/Qwen3-8B")`, `renderer = renderers.get_renderer("qwen3", tokenizer)`.
- Renderer name for Qwen3-8B with thinking DISABLED: `"qwen3_disable_thinking"`. The Renderer class docs say: "qwen3 ...assistant\n<think>\n open, so False; qwen3_disable_thinking ...assistant\n<think>\n\n</think>\n\n closed, so True". Note that "qwen3_8_disable_thinking" is for Qwen3.8, not Qwen3-8B. Do not use qwen3_5/qwen3_8 names for Qwen3-8B.
- get_recommended_renderer_name(model_name): "Return the most recommended renderer for the model." The page does not list a value for Qwen/Qwen3-8B. NOT FOUND.
- Renderer.build_generation_prompt(messages, role, prefill): returns `tinker.ModelInput`. Example from rendering tutorial: `prompt = renderer.build_generation_prompt(messages[:-1])`.
- Renderer.get_stop_sequences(): "Return stop token IDs or strings that signal end-of-generation for the model." Returns `list[str] | list[int]`. Tutorial output for Qwen3.5/3.6 was `[248046]` = `<|im_end|>`.
- Renderer.build_supervised_example(messages, train_on_what): returns `tuple[tinker.ModelInput, torch.Tensor]` — "A `(model_input, weights)` tuple where weights is a 1-D float tensor". So NOT a plain tokens list.
- Renderer.build_supervised_examples(messages, train_on_what) (plural): returns a list of (ModelInput, weight tensor) tuples; used "when the renderer does not satisfy the extension property".
- TrainOnWhat values [summary]: LAST_ASSISTANT_MESSAGE (default), LAST_ASSISTANT_TURN, ALL_ASSISTANT_MESSAGES, ALL_MESSAGES, ALL_TOKENS, CUSTOMIZED.
- Helper to convert a conversation to a Datum (conversation_to_datum / datum_from_model_input_weights): NOT FOUND in the pages read. The rendering tutorial page explicitly does not mention them [summary]. Build the Datum by hand from ModelInput plus weights (shift as in section 3). Note that ModelInput.from_ints is shown in the cheatsheet; a ModelInput built by the renderer is also a valid `model_input`.
- Pickling: "Renderers created via `get_renderer()` are automatically pickleable."

8. Pricing (Models & Pricing page)
- "All prices are per million tokens. Checkpoint storage is charged at $0.10 per GB per month."
- "We provide an 80% discount on cached prefill tokens."
- Qwen3-8B row (verbatim from summary): "[Qwen3-8B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-8B) 32K 8B 8B Dense Hybrid Qwen/Qwen3-8B $0.195$0.039 (cached) $0.60 $0.44"
- Mapping, by column order: Prefill = $0.195 per 1M (cached $0.039); Sample = $0.60 per 1M; Train = $0.44 per 1M. The page's verbatim header text for the three price columns was cut off, so this mapping is [inferred] from column order. The Serverless table headers say "Prefill (Input)" and "Sample (Output)". The page calls train "Forward and backward pass for gradient computation."

9. Usage and spend
- CLI: `tinker billing usage STARTING_ON ENDING_BEFORE` — "Show hourly billing usage for your organization." Timestamps are RFC 3339, UTC-hour aligned (e.g. 2026-07-13T00:00:00Z), at most 14 days apart. Options: `--csv PATH`, `--sessions-csv PATH`. Requires billing view access. Costs are "estimated gross USD usage cost before credits and commits... These are not invoice amounts due." Data lags "by up to a few hours."
- CLI: `tinker billing checkpoint-storage [--project-id TEXT] [--csv PATH]` — checkpoint storage; "Checkpoint usage data can lag by 1-2 hours."
- Console: quickstart links https://tinker.thinkingmachines.ai/billing/ and https://tinker.thinkingmachines.ai/sessions ("View Sessions in the Tinker Console"). Session metrics page not read.
- SDK: BillingUsageResponse and GetBillingUsageRequest types exist (index sidebar); details not read.

10. Rate limits and concurrency
- NOT FOUND: no rate-limit numbers or concurrency caps in the cheatsheet, SamplingClient, or TrainingClient pages read.
- Guidance from the cheatsheet "Concurrent Requests": use `num_samples=16` for many samples from one prompt; for different prompts, `asyncio.gather(sampling_client.sample_async(...), ...)`. Pipelining: `optim_step(...)` can be issued while the next `forward_backward_async` runs. See "Clock Cycles & Pipelining" (tinker/under-the-hood) for throughput; not read.
- Exceptions include RateLimitError (tinker._exceptions); details not read.
- Subprocess sampling: "set `TINKER_SUBPROCESS_SAMPLING=1`" to run sample()/compute_logprobs() in a subprocess.

CAVEATS
- Signatures for sample(), forward_backward(), optim_step(), save_weights_for_sampler() came from [summary] of long pages, but the signature text matches the API reference.

- Checkpoints howto recommends weights-format and export guidance (merge or PEFT) for use outside Tinker; not needed for sampling inside Tinker.

- "A `Datum` is a single training example. It contains input tokens, target tokens, and per-token loss weights (0 = ignore, 1 = compute loss). Position `i` of the input predicts token `i + 1`"
- Code:
  full_sequence = prompt_tokens + completion_tokens
  n_prefix = len(prompt_tokens) - 1
  datum = types.Datum(
      model_input=types.ModelInput.from_ints(tokens=full_sequence[:-1]),
      loss_fn_inputs=dict(
          weights=[0.0] * n_prefix + [1.0] * len(completion_tokens),  # 0 for prompt, 1 for completion
          target_tokens=full_sequence[1:],  # shifted by 1 from input
      )
  )
- So loss_fn_inputs keys are `weights` and `target_tokens`. In the cheatsheet they are plain Python lists of float and int. Whether TensorData or numpy is also accepted is NOT VERIFIED (Datum and TensorData pages not read).
- Note: the renderer's build_supervised_example returns weights as a torch.Tensor (see section 7). The cheatsheet passes lists. Convert with .tolist() if needed (inference).
- RL variant: target_tokens, logprobs, advantages keys.

4. optim_step and AdamParams
- Signature: `optim_step(optim_params=None, adam_params=None)`. Returns "APIFuture containing optimizer step response". adam_params is "a legacy alias and cannot be combined with `optim_params`" [summary].
- Cheatsheet: `await training_client.optim_step_async(types.AdamParams(learning_rate=1e-4))` then `await optim_future.result_async()`. Quickstart: `tinker.AdamParams(learning_rate=2e-4)`.
- AdamParams fields (verbatim field names): learning_rate (float, "Learning rate for the optimizer"), beta1 (float), beta2 (float), eps (float, "Term added to the denominator to improve numerical stability"), weight_decay (float, "Uses decoupled weight decay."), grad_clip_norm (float, "0.0 means no clipping."). Defaults NOT shown on the page.

5. Saving weights
- `training_client.save_weights_for_sampler(name, ttl_seconds=None, user_metadata=None)` returns an APIFuture; result has `.path`. Path format: `tinker://<run_id>/sampler_weights/<name>`. Example: `sampler_checkpoint = training_client.save_weights_for_sampler("step-100", ...).result()`; `print(sampler_checkpoint.path)  # tinker://<run_id>/sampler_weights/step-100`. Async: `save_weights_for_sampler_async(name="first-sft")`.
- `training_client.save_weights_and_get_sampling_client(name=None, retry_config=None, record_stability_info=False)` returns a SamplingClient "configured with the current model weights". Per API ref, `name` is "Deprecated, has no effect. Will be removed in a future release." CONFLICT: the cheatsheet still shows `save_weights_and_get_sampling_client(name="checkpoint-1")`. Treat name as optional and ignored.
- `training_client.save_state(name, ttl_seconds=None, overwrite=False, user_metadata=None)` returns APIFuture with `.path` in `tinker://<run_id>/weights/<name>` (full state incl. optimizer). `load_state(path, weights_access_token=None)` loads weights only.
- Checkpoints howto table: "save_state | Resume training | `tinker://<run_id>/weights/<name>`" and "save_weights_for_sampler | Sample, open in the Playground, or download | `tinker://<run_id>/sampler_weights/<name>`".
- Load for sampling: `service_client.create_sampling_client(model_path=sampler_checkpoint.path)`.
- Resume training: `service_client.create_training_client_from_state(path)` (weights only) and `create_training_client_from_state_with_optimizer(path)`.
- Storage: "Checkpoint storage is charged at $0.10 per GB per month."

6. Sampling
- `sampling_client.sample(prompt, num_samples, sampling_params, include_prompt_logprobs=False, topk_prompt_logprobs=0, topk_sample_logprobs=0, target_prompt_logprobs=None, prompt_alt_tokens_k=0, prompt_logprobs_last_n=None)` returns a Future containing SampleResponse [summary for signature].
- Cheatsheet (async): 
  prompt = types.ModelInput.from_ints(tokenizer.encode("The capital of France is"))
  params = types.SamplingParams(max_tokens=50, temperature=0.7, stop=["\n"])
  result = await sampling_client.sample_async(prompt=prompt, num_samples=1, sampling_params=params)
  print(tokenizer.decode(result.sequences[0].tokens))
- Cheatsheet: "sample_async returns the result directly". Sync form per API ref: `future = sampling_client.sample(prompt=prompt, sampling_params=params, num_samples=1)`; `result = future.result()`.
- SampledSequence fields per quickstart: "Each sample in the result's `sequences` has its `tokens`, the `logprobs` of those tokens, and a `stop_reason`", where stop_reason is "stop" or "length".
- SamplingParams fields (verbatim): max_tokens (Optional[int], "Maximum number of tokens to generate"), seed (Optional[int]), stop (Union[str, Sequence[str], Sequence[int], None], "`None` keeps implicit EOS stopping; `[]` disables all stop tokens, including EOS"), temperature (float), top_k (int, "-1 for no limit"), top_p (float).
- compute_logprobs(prompt, prompt_logprobs_last_n=None) returns a Future of a list; `compute_logprobs_async(prompt)` returns the result directly.

7. Renderers (tinker_cookbook)
- Imports: `from tinker_cookbook import renderers`; `from tinker_cookbook.tokenizer_utils import get_tokenizer`.
- `get_tokenizer(model_name)`: "Get a tokenizer by name." Example: `tokenizer = get_tokenizer("Qwen/Qwen3-8B")`.
- `renderers.get_renderer(name, tokenizer, image_processor, model_name)`: "Factory function to create renderers by name." Parameter `name` docstring list includes: `"qwen3"`: Qwen3 with thinking enabled; `"qwen3_disable_thinking"`: Qwen3 with thinking disabled; `"qwen3_instruct"`: Qwen3 instruct 2507 (no thinking); `"qwen3_8_disable_thinking"`: Qwen3.8 with thinking disabled. image_processor is "Required for VL renderers." Example from docs: `tokenizer = get_tokenizer("Qwen/Qwen3-8B")`, `renderer = renderers.get_renderer("qwen3", tokenizer)`.
- Renderer name for Qwen3-8B with thinking DISABLED: `"qwen3_disable_thinking"`. The Renderer class docs say: "qwen3 ...assistant\n<think>\n open, so False; qwen3_disable_thinking ...assistant\n<think>\n\n</think>\n\n closed, so True". Note that "qwen3_8_disable_thinking" is for Qwen3.8, not Qwen3-8B. Do not use qwen3_5/qwen3_8 names for Qwen3-8B.
- get_recommended_renderer_name(model_name): "Return the most recommended renderer for the model." The page does not list a value for Qwen/Qwen3-8B. NOT FOUND.
- Renderer.build_generation_prompt(messages, role, prefill): returns `tinker.ModelInput`. Example from rendering tutorial: `prompt = renderer.build_generation_prompt(messages[:-1])`.
- Renderer.get_stop_sequences(): "Return stop token IDs or strings that signal end-of-generation for the model." Returns `list[str] | list[int]`. Tutorial output for Qwen3.5/3.6 was `[248046]` = `<|im_end|>`.
- Renderer.build_supervised_example(messages, train_on_what): returns `tuple[tinker.ModelInput, torch.Tensor]` — "A `(model_input, weights)` tuple where weights is a 1-D float tensor". So NOT a plain tokens list.
- Renderer.build_supervised_examples(messages, train_on_what) (plural): returns a list of (ModelInput, weight tensor) tuples; used "when the renderer does not satisfy the extension property".
- TrainOnWhat values [summary]: LAST_ASSISTANT_MESSAGE (default), LAST_ASSISTANT_TURN, ALL_ASSISTANT_MESSAGES, ALL_MESSAGES, ALL_TOKENS, CUSTOMIZED.
- Helper to convert a conversation to a Datum (conversation_to_datum / datum_from_model_input_weights): NOT FOUND in the pages read. The rendering tutorial page explicitly does not mention them [summary]. Build the Datum by hand from ModelInput plus weights (shift as in section 3). Note that ModelInput.from_ints is shown in the cheatsheet; a ModelInput built by the renderer is also a valid `model_input`.
- Pickling: "Renderers created via `get_renderer()` are automatically pickleable."

9. Usage and spend
- CLI: `tinker billing usage STARTING_ON ENDING_BEFORE` — "Show hourly billing usage for your organization." Timestamps are RFC 3339, UTC-hour aligned (e.g. 2026-07-13T00:00:00Z), at most 14 days apart. Options: `--csv PATH`, `--sessions-csv PATH`. Requires billing view access. Costs are "estimated gross USD usage cost before credits and commits... These are not invoice amounts due." Data lags "by up to a few hours."
